# Forge

> Strongly typed state transitions, explainable strategy decisions and structured test expectations for .NET 10.

Forge is an MIT-licensed .NET library family by Pjotr Casteel.

Canonical website: https://pjotrcasteel.github.io/Forge/
Canonical repository: https://github.com/pjotrcasteel/Forge

## Packages

- Forge.Delta — source-generated semantic object differences.
  - NuGet: https://www.nuget.org/packages/Forge.Delta
- Forge.Sync — source-generated desired-state reconciliation and typed planning. Depends on Forge.Delta.
  - NuGet: https://www.nuget.org/packages/Forge.Sync
- Forge.Parse — structured JSON expectation matching for dynamic test output.
  - NuGet: https://www.nuget.org/packages/Forge.Parse
- Forge.Parse.Reqnroll — optional Reqnroll DataTable adapter over Forge.Parse.
  - NuGet: https://www.nuget.org/packages/Forge.Parse.Reqnroll
- Forge.Decide — typed strategy spaces, side-effect-free proposals, deterministic selection, explanations, shadow decisions, receipts and evidence diffing.
  - NuGet: https://www.nuget.org/packages/Forge.Decide
- Forge.Decide.Testing — framework-neutral scenario matrices for finding uncovered and ambiguous decision contexts.
  - NuGet: https://www.nuget.org/packages/Forge.Decide.Testing
- Forge.Decide.DependencyInjection — explicit Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection adapter for typed strategy spaces; no assembly scanning.
  - NuGet: https://www.nuget.org/packages/Forge.Decide.DependencyInjection
- Forge.Decide.OpenTelemetry — ActivitySource instrumentation for Decide without owning OpenTelemetry providers or exporters.
  - NuGet: https://www.nuget.org/packages/Forge.Decide.OpenTelemetry

Current family version: 1.20.0

## Core boundary

Forge calculates, classifies, validates, explains and simulates transitions and decisions.
Forge does not persist state, call external systems, publish messages, authorize actions or execute plans.
Forge.Decide owns decision mechanics; the consumer owns domain meaning, authority and side effects.

## Important semantics

- Delta answers: what changed inside one object?
- Sync answers: how do keyed current and desired collections differ?
- Parse answers: does dynamic structured output satisfy the expectation that matters?
- Decide answers: which valid course of action should become the plan, and why?
- A Decide strategy space is a hard candidate boundary. Strategies outside the space are not evaluated.
- Decide strategies propose application-owned plans without executing them.
- Decide evaluates proposals before selection so production and shadow policies can operate on the same frozen evidence.
- Decide does not silently resolve ambiguity by registration order; the default requires exactly one applicable proposal.
- Replace means complete desired state; current-only items may be removed.
- Upsert means partial desired input; current-only items are preserved.
- Generated normal hot paths use direct property access rather than runtime reflection.
- Logical keys, execution states, facts, reasons, approval scopes and invariant violations remain consumer CLR types.
- Portable manifests and decision receipts are data, not executable code.
